requirements.text: It needs to be prioritized as Critical immediately.

requirements.source: Case CS-0000001 now owned by Stephanie in CSM Tier 1 with Critical priority
assumptions: CS-0000001 is case 1 (contact 123, Elizabeth Chase; product 128, Palo Alto Networks PA-3220)
weak: case 1 is already critical on the seed, so the requirement only guards against the priority being lowered

assumptions: Stephanie Todd is user 6, an active agent; the previous owner Susan Garcia is user 403, assigned_to on the seed in group 4 (Case Assignment)

requirements.text: Make the assignment and group updates now.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 1 AND assignment_group_id = 1
requirements.source: Case CS-0000001 now owned by Stephanie in CSM Tier 1 with Critical priority
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy requires the assignee to be a member of the assignment group, and CSM Tier 1 Support (group 1) is the only group Stephanie Todd is to remain in
CSM Tier 1 Support is group 1; CSM Tier 1 Support_2, _3 and _4 are other groups

requirements.text: please ensure she is added to the CSM Tier 1 Support group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE member_id = 960 AND group_id = 1 AND user_id = 6
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest member_id 959); this is the only membership the task creates
Stephanie Todd is not a member of group 1 on the seed
group 1 is CSM Tier 1 Support exactly, not the similarly named CSM Tier 1 Support_2, _3 or _4

requirements.text: ensure she is removed from any other groups she is currently part of
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group_member WHERE user_id = 6 AND group_id <> 1
requirements.source: Stephanie has no other group memberships
assumptions: on the seed she belongs to Installed Base Support_3 (group 50, inactive, member 298) and Returns Authorization Desk_2 (group 35, member 659); both are removed

disagreement: selector and cells: A selector user_id = 6 with cell group_id <> 1, B selector user_id = 6 AND group_id <> 1 with no cells; same sql and the same two rows on the seed; chose B's because the selector then names exactly the memberships that must be gone, which is what a remove requirement counts

requirements.text: The previous owner, Susan Garcia, has left the company.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "user" WHERE user_id = 403 AND active = 0
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: a user who has left the company is deactivated, and a tool that updates user details is available
Susan Garcia is user 403 (susan.garcia@servicenow.com), active on the seed
the acting user Karen Watkins (user 39) is an admin, the role the policy allows to deactivate users

disagreement: sql: A quotes the table name as "user", B leaves it bare; both return the same count on the seed; chose the quoted form because user is a reserved word in many SQL dialects and the benchmark's own check quotes it

notes:
No benchmark check tests Stephanie Todd's membership of CSM Tier 1 Support (the benchmark's membership check passes with no memberships at all), so it is a new requirement.
The case's priority is already critical on the seed, so that requirement is weak; the benchmark's case check as a whole is not, since the owner and group change.
Stephanie Todd owns two other cases on the seed: CS-0000525 (in_progress, group 50) and CS-0000472 (canceled, group 35). Removing her from those groups leaves her assigned outside her groups, which the policy's assignment rule does not allow, but the request asks nothing about those cases, so no requirement is written for them.
Susan Garcia's own membership of Case Assignment (group 4) is not mentioned by the request and is not tested.

disagreement: value: the removal of Stephanie Todd's other memberships: one pass puts group_id <> 1 in the cells, the other in the selector, with the same sql; chose the selector form because it names exactly the memberships that must be gone.
